items.title: Ethiopian Airlines launches direct flight to Nacala
items.summary: Maputo, 28 Oct (AIM) – State-owned Company Ethiopian Airlines has launched direct flights to the port city of Nacala, northern Mozambican province of Nampula, opening up new opportunities for tourism, trade, and investment. On Tuesday, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft landed at Nacala International Airport at 14:25, after a stopover in Blantyre, Malawi. Nacala becomes the airline’s third destination in Mozambique, joining southern Maputo and central city of Beira, in Sofala province. The new service operates on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, connecting Nacala to Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa. Passengers will gain access to the airline’s international network, which serves more than 130 destinations worldwide. Nampula Provincial Governor, Eduardo Abdula, described the new connection as a sign of confidence in Mozambique’s economic potential, highlighting Nacala’s geographical position and port infrastructure as important assets for regional trade.

items.title: Mozambique signs agreement with China to restructure its debt
items.summary: Maputo, 28 Oct (AIM) – Mozambique’s public debt with China will be restructured following the signing of a Supplementary Framework Agreement between the governments’ of both countries. The agreement follows meetings held in China last April between Mozambican President Daniel Chapo and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, in which China granted a partial forgiveness of Mozambique’s debt, amounting to 204 million yuan (1.9 billion meticais) in interest-free loans that were set to mature in December 2024. The agreement was signed by the finance minister Carla Louveira and the Chinese ambassador to Mozambique Zheng Xuan. The agreement aligns with the Medium-Term Public Debt Management Strategy (2025–2029) and represents a significant step toward aligning debt repayments with the country’s financial capacity, thereby strengthening the sustainability of public finances.

items.title: Kremlin: Conversation with President of Mozambique Daniel Francisco Chapo
items.summary: President of Russia Vladimir Putin : Mister President, I am very glad to see you. At the outset, I want to say that we greatly appreciate your personal active participation in the Russia-Africa summit. It is important that Mozambique was represented at the top level in the previous Russian-African forums as well, which, in my opinion, laid a good foundation for Russia to develop ties with the entire continent Today, we have worked productively with you at the 8th Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum We completely share your commitment to strengthening multifaceted ties between our countries. Russia and Mozambique are connected by long-standing bonds of friendship established way back at the time of struggle for independence by the people of Mozambique. Last year we marked an important anniversary – 50 years of our diplomatic relations Our political contacts and interparliamentary ties are progressing.

items.title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
items.summary: The Villa Vie Odyssey was more than 750 days into its voyage around the world when it came to a stop in Cambodia A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world said it suspended operations due to extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia The US-based operator of Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and "temporary living arrangements" It is unclear how many were on board but the nearly 200m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers. It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a "continuous voyage around the world" Global fuel prices have soared since the Iran war started earlier this year. The ship's operator said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 (£6,000) from $1,800 The company said it had taken "significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port".

items.title: Arab parties could hold key as Netanyahu and Eisenkot set to fall short of victory
items.summary: Arab parties could end up holding the balance of power With results still trickling in, it currently appears that Israel's veteran Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has done better than was widely predicted with his Likud emerging as the largest single party His existing bloc with ultra-nationalist and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties appear to be just short of a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat parliament. However, analysts caution that this is subject to change because the early count was skewed towards areas known to have strong right-wing support A dramatic deadlock had been widely forecast as Israelis surged to the polls – with turnout reaching more than 77% In Israel's fragmented political system, the signs are that Netanyahu's main rival, the former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, would struggle to command a parliamentary majority without parties led by Israel's Arab minority.
